**From left to right**, the **exact values** of the $x$-intercepts of the parabola shown above are{{field-1}}and{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-1,3)$ and passes through the point $(-2,\frac{5}{2}).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-1,3)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =4p(y-3).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-2,\frac{5}{2}),$ we substitute $x=-2$ and $y=\frac{5}{2}$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2+1)^{2} & =4p(\frac{5}{2}-3) \\ (-1)^{2} & =4p(-\frac{1}{2}) \\ 1 & =-2p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =-2(y-3).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2} & =-2(0-3) \\ (x+1)^{2} & =6 \\ x+1 & =\pm \sqrt{6} \\ x & =-1\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $-1-\sqrt{6}$ and $-1+\sqrt{6}.$
